newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian L&H says it ready for the future.
newsitem.headline: Belgian L&H says it ready for the future.

text.p: Lernout & Hauspie Speech Products NV, a Belgian speech technology firm listed on Nasdaq, said on Tuesday that with the speech market moving from an emerging to a growth stage it was confident it was ready for the future.

"The achievements of the fourth quarter of 1996 clearly indicate that the new structure of L&H is working," Jo Lernout, co-founder and co-chairman, said in a statement on fourth quarter and full year 1996 earnings.
In the fourth quarter L&H integrated Mendez translation, bought in September 1996 for $16.9 million, and acquired Berkeley Speech Technologies of the U.S..
It said a major fourth quarter highlight was the increase in recurring licensing and engineering revenues from core speech technologies to $2.0 million from $0.4 million in the third quarter.

"1996 was an important milestone. During its first year on Nasdaq the company signed 65 significant agreements, including ones with industry leaders such as Microsoft and Hitachi," said president Gaston Bastiaens.
Revenues quadrupled to $31.01 million. "The company came into solid profit," he added. Pre-tax profit before write-offs rose to $24.33 million from $5.23 million.
